findings.why: An unhedged claim to reduce acne sits on the cosmetic/drug line and needs a legal check; it is on the product page (F2) but no study for it is attached. If legal reads it as treating a condition it becomes a CLM-01 disease claim, and it is also unhedged efficacy (LNG-04).
findings.fix: Gently exfoliates and smoothens skin, formulated for acne-prone body skin, without compromising the skin barrier.

findings.span: Salicylic Acid ~58% vs LHA 6% penetration of the outer layer
findings.why: These penetration percentages are factual figures shown with no source on the creative; they come from ingredient literature on the product page (F14, F15), not from a test of this body wash.
findings.fix: Add a footnote citing the source of the 58% and 6% penetration figures, or remove the numbers and keep 'Salicylic Acid works deep; LHA exfoliates the outer layer'.

tone_read: Calm and ingredient-led: it names both actives, the 2% strength and how each works at a different depth, with a clear routine. No fear hooks, hype or emoji; it sounds like Minimalist.
language_read: The concentration and actives match the product exactly. The one language slip is 'reduces body acne', an unhedged outcome claim where the brand would normally scope to acne-prone skin, and the penetration figures need a source.
